# Draft:From Lecture Hall to Jubilee House: The Rise of Ghanaʻs First Woman Vice President

From Lecture Hall to Jubilee House: The Rise of Ghana's First Woman Vice President is a Ghanaian academic and politician who assumed office as the first female Vice President of Ghana on January 7, 2025. She started a journey as a academic practician (Teacher) and later became a Minister Of Education from 2013 to 2017 and now Ghana's 8th Vice President.
Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang served as the Chancellor of the Women’s University in Africa from 2018 to 2024.
At the University of Cape Coast, Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang held several key leadership positions, including: Head of the department of English, dean of the Faculty of Arts, Dean of the Board of Graduate Studies, Founding Dean of the School of Graduate Studies and Research and Vice-Chancellor (the first woman to hold that position at UCC).Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang
In addition, she was a two-time recipient of the prestigious Fulbright Program scholarship, which highlights her global academic recognition and contribution to research and education.
Her career reflects a strong commitment to academic excellence, leadership, and the advancement of higher education, especially for women in Africa.[https://whoswhoghana.app/power-ladies/professor-jane-naana-opoku-agyemang/#:~:text=Professor%20Jane%20Naana%20Opoku%20Agyemang,in%201980%20and%201986%2C%20respectively.]
Ahead of the 2012 general elections, Jane Opoku Agyemang served as the moderator of the IEA Presidential debate with Kojo Oppong Nkrumah the current Minister of Information.
AWARDS
# Officer of the order of the Volta (For Academic Distinction)
# Doctor of Letters, University of Cape Coast
# Ghana Women Of Excellence Award (Education)
# Doctor of Humane Letters, Grand Valley State University, Michigan, USA (Honoris Causa)
# Global Leadership Award, University of South Florida, USA
# Doctor of Humane Letters, Winston Salem State University, North California, USA
# Doctor of Laws, University of the West Indies (Honoris Causa)
# Twice recognized for outstanding Performance in Advancing International Education school for International, Vermont, USA
